description: Issue #1223: slat axis 212 deg, 22/20 cm slats, drive turns to 125 deg, summer solstice at 47.5N. Midday sun along the axis needs more than 125 deg on the facing side, so the roof must close from the other face, then fall into the normal far-side pose once the sun passes the axis.
Same roof and day with the fallback off: the clamp pins the slats at 125 deg and sun leaks through (blocked = false) in the window the fallback fixes.
Same roof, margin 0: the roof stays on the facing side right up to 125 deg and only switches once the facing angle is unreachable.
Same roof, margin 10: the switch fires 10 deg before the limit.
A 0-90 deg drive (no max_slat_angle): facing-side sun that needs more than vertical would leave the slats fully open; the roof closes from the other face.
A 160 deg drive reaches every facing-side angle needed here, so the fallback never engages.
Slats run north-south (axis 0): sun swinging through south, at several heights.
Same north-south slats described by axis 180 (the roof faces the other way).
Slats run east-west (axis 90): sun swinging through east, at several heights.
Slats on a 45 deg diagonal, 100 deg drive.
Different slat geometry: 30 cm slats at 25 cm spacing, 120 deg drive.
Slats as wide as their spacing (20 cm at 20 cm): no interlock overlap, so the nominal chord applies. 135 deg drive.
